case_scope: Supplied synthetic brief only; no case traces or route records supplied.

sources.title: Recommended International Code of Practice for Packaging and Transport of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables
sources.publisher: Codex Alimentarius Commission / FAO-hosted official PDF
sources.released_version: CAC/RCP 44-1995, Amendment 1-2004; official combined text, no later edition asserted
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the official PDF text at pp. 152-156. It advises pre-cooling when needed; checking air circulation and equipment; documenting small air-logger location in a likely warm zone; and gives an illustrative top/side/rear placement.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Recommendations are conditional on produce, equipment, mode, external conditions, volume, transit time, and commodity compatibility. It explicitly requires airflow under/around/through a load; pre-cooling if needed; mixed loads require compatibility; logger position is a warm-air sampling recommendation, not a product-temperature proxy.
sources.applicability: Primary transport/packaging mechanism and implementation-history anchor. Useful for measurement location and handling questions, not a binding local rule, safe limit, or proof of case-specific practice.

sources.title: The role of post-harvest management in assuring the quality and safety of horticultural produce
sources.released_version: FAO web text; page presents chapter 3; publication/version date not stated on retrieved page
sources.observed_operation: Opened the full text. It says packaging influences airflow, commodity rather than air temperature should be measured, loading/air spaces affect cooling, and mixed commodities can require compromise.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Advice is general postharvest guidance and commodity-specific; it does not establish this cooperative's product set or operating conditions.
sources.applicability: Supports product-versus-air distinction and need to measure initial/product state; not used for any numeric safety or quality threshold.

sources.title: Section 6: Temperature and relative humidity control
sources.released_version: Web chapter; cited underlying guidance includes Kader 1992; page edition date not stated
sources.locator: Sections on cooling and RH, especially lines 16-27 and 40-48
sources.observed_operation: Opened the full text. It describes conduction/convection/radiation/evaporation, shade and alternative cooling concepts; warns that liners can impede efficient cooling and that vent alignment matters.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Alternative methods and RH/temperature needs vary by commodity; ice/evaporative cooling are only appropriate for some products. Added package materials can slow cooling.
sources.applicability: Mechanism source for passive packaging/preconditioning alternatives and risks; no claim that any method fits unknown produce.

sources.title: Real-Time Temperature and Humidity Measurements during the Short-Range Distribution of Perishable Food Products as a Tool for Supply-Chain Energy Improvements
sources.released_version: Processes 2022, 10(11), 2286; version of record published 4 November 2022 per publisher article-versions notes
sources.locator: Methods §§2.2-2.3 and sensor/load placement; reported five-stop short-range Portugal route and in-crate sensors; indexed full-text result
sources.observed_operation: Searched the exact title/DOI and read publisher-indexed result snippets and article-version notes. Opening the full article endpoint returned HTTP 429, so no full article page was read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported route used a refrigerated van, 18 wireless T/RH sensors near diverse crate contents, five stops and roughly 4.5 hours; a vehicle setpoint and a single route do not isolate causal effects. Sensor readings near produce are not automatically product-core or quality readings.
sources.applicability: Comparable implementation history for contextualized route/stop/package measurement. Results do not predict this route or justify an intervention.

sources.title: Thermal Management of Short-Range Distribution of Perishable Food Products Using Phase Change Materials in Packaging: Real-Time Field Data Acquisition
sources.released_version: Energies 2023, 16(13), 5191; version of record published 5 July 2023; publisher notes list later HTML file updates
sources.locator: Methods §§2.1-2.4 and results/discussion; route, crate comparison, and sensor details retrieved from indexed publisher search result; Notes page confirms version history
sources.observed_operation: Read publisher Notes/version history and indexed publisher article snippets; direct full HTML fetch returned HTTP 429.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One orange-crate field route in Portugal, winter, 8:00-14:05, six stops, refrigeration switched off, ambient about 1-10°C; comparison was PCM alveoli vs empty alveoli, with small ventilated air sensors. PCM buffering is finite; authors call for future work on autonomy and amount under specific conditions. Index reports phase change not fully finished by journey end.
sources.applicability: Relevant passive-package field analogue showing both possible buffering and context/finite-autonomy limits. It does not prove core-temperature, quality, or powered-cooling benefits for this unknown product/route.

sources.title: Artificial fruit for monitoring the thermal history of horticultural produce in the cold chain
sources.released_version: Journal of Food Engineering 215 (December 2017), pp. 51-60; DOI record/version of record
sources.locator: Abstract and study summary: prototype method and apple cooling comparison; search-indexed publisher result
sources.observed_operation: Read the publisher-indexed abstract and bibliographic result. Direct article fetch returned HTTP 403.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Prototype mimicked apple thermal response; compared with ten real apples during cooling, reporting cooling time within 5%; water-filled surrogates differed up to 16%. This is a specific surrogate/product and cooling test.
sources.applicability: Supports considering a crop-matched thermal surrogate for repeatable placement; does not validate an off-the-shelf/generic surrogate for unknown produce.

sources.title: Adoption challenges of environmental monitoring practices: case study of temperature data loggers in selected Australian vegetable supply chains
sources.released_version: Applied Water Science 14, article 260 (2024); version of record published 23 November 2024
sources.locator: Results §§existing monitoring practices and adoption factors; full publisher article lines 245-277 and 282-304, 340
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read publisher full-text page. Study reports purposively selected qualitative cases and interview-based analysis.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Three selected Australian vegetable chains; findings include logger cost/retrieval labor, mixed-crop compatibility, low sharing and responsibility/accountability barriers. These are reported contexts, not universal effects or cooperative-specific facts.
sources.applicability: Implementation-history comparator for including labor, data retrieval, ownership, and traceability cost in the pilot.
